_comment: Which rail each capacitor sits on, and what that rail runs at.
The rated voltage is NOT here -- it is read from the parts list
at run time, so a corrected BOM corrects this too.
All 25 capacitors on the board are audited. Every net was traced on
schematic sheet 1; what varies is whether the *voltage* on that net is
published. So source is used strictly:
'schematic'  the net was traced on the sheet AND Table 2-2 or §2-25…§2-29
states what that net runs at. These are the regulated rails.
'inferred'   the net was traced on the sheet, but nothing in the manuals
states its voltage and the sheet does not annotate it -- the
+35VUR node carries TP4 and nothing else. The figure is
derived, and each note says from what. Do not read these as
measurements; they are design points good to perhaps 20%.
The four unregulated rails were derived like this:
+75VUR ~100 V   73 V out through a Darlington emitter follower needs real
headroom, and R6 (10 k, 2 W) across the rail dissipates
1.0 W at 100 V -- half its rating, which is where a bleeder
is normally sized. C1 is a 160 V part, consistent.
+35VUR ~45 V    35 V out through Q5 (TIP120) plus headroom; R13 (10 k,
0.25 W) bleeds it and would be at 81% of rating at 45 V,
which caps how high it can plausibly be. C3 is 100 V.
±12VUR ~18 V    a 7812/7912 pair needs about 14.5 V in, and C6/C7 are 25 V
parts -- 18 V is the usual design point between the two.
+5VUR  ~8.5 V   U3 is a low-dropout type feeding 5.2 V, and C12/C13 are
16 V parts.
The ac-side capacitors are entered at the peak of their winding, which for a
capacitor-input rectifier is the dc rail plus the rectifier drop.
railClass is how much energy is behind the rail, which decides what a shorted
part does. These letters are this board's:
A  an unregulated reservoir node. Behind its supply fuse, but the whole
reservoir is behind it too -- 22 000 µF on +5VUR, 10 000 µF on +12VUR --
so a short here dumps the bank before the fuse can clear. The worst
place on this assembly for a capacitor to fail short.
B  the output of a three-terminal IC regulator (U1, U2, U3): current
limited and thermally protected, so a short is survivable.
C  the output of a discrete series-pass regulator (Q1/Q3, or Q5) with a
resistive current limit and no thermal protection.
D  the ac side of a rectifier, ahead of the reservoir. The part sees the
winding's peak in both polarities, and a short is across a transformer
secondary through that supply's own fuse.
There are no tantalums on this board. Every electrolytic is aluminium, which
is why Recap ranks these by capacitance lost rather than by voltage margin --
but the margins are here because a 1987 can on 72% of its rating is worth
knowing about before it is refitted.
Hand-authored; tools/import_cap_audit.py was not used.

C6.note: Reservoir for the unregulated +12 V rail, from rectifier CR17–CR20 and fused by F3 (§2-26). Sheet 1. The 18 V is derived from the 7812's input requirement and the part's own 25 V rating; nothing publishes it. The tightest margin on the board, together with C7 — a 25 V can on an 18 V rail is about 72%, so fit 35 V parts when recapping.

C7.note: Reservoir for the unregulated -12 V rail, same rectifier as C6, fused by F4 (§2-26). Sheet 1. Negative with respect to COMMON; entered as a magnitude. Same 72% as C6. Table 6-24 prints its tolerance as +-20%.25V and the Rev 9 list as +30-20%,25V — the 25 V rating is the same either way.

C1.note: Reservoir for the unregulated +75 V rail, from rectifier CR1–CR4 and fused by F1, bled by R6 (§2-28). Sheet 1. The 100 V is derived from R6's 2 W rating at 10 k and from the 73 V output plus Darlington headroom; the manuals publish nothing for this node. Holds the most energy of any capacitor here at working voltage — give R6 several seconds after power-down.

C12.note: Half the +5 V reservoir with C13, from rectifier CR25–CR28 and fused at 3.15 A by F5 (§2-25). Sheet 1. The 8.5 V is derived from U3 being a low-dropout type feeding 5.2 V and from the part's own 16 V rating. 22 000 µF behind no further protection than F5 — the highest stored charge on the board.

C13.note: The other half of the +5 V reservoir, in parallel with C12. Sheet 1. Same derivation, same rail, same margin.

C4.note: Bypass on the regulated +35 V output, after Q5 (§2-27). Sheet 1. 35 V is Table 2-2's nominal for TP5. A 63 V part at 56% — the tightest of the regulated-rail capacitors.

C3.note: Reservoir for the unregulated +35 V rail, from rectifier CR9–CR12 and fused by F2, bled by R13 (§2-27). Sheet 1. The 45 V is derived: it must clear 35 V plus Q5's headroom, and R13 (10 k, 0.25 W) would be running at 81% of rating there, which is about as high as it can plausibly sit.

C2.note: Bypass on the regulated +75 V output, after the Q3/Q1 Darlington (§2-28). Sheet 1. 73 V is Table 2-2's nominal for TP2 — the circuit's own figure, VR6 + VR7 less two base-emitter drops.

C15.note: On the regulated +5 V output of U3 (§2-25). Sheet 1. 5.2 V is Table 2-2's nominal for TP12, lifted from 5.0 V by the germanium diode CR35.

C10.note: Bypass on U2's regulated -12 V output (§2-26). Sheet 1. Entered as a magnitude.

C8.note: In parallel with C7 on the unregulated -12 V rail — the sheet puts it on U2's input side, although §2-26 groups it with the output bypasses C10 and C19. Sheet 1. Same derived 18 V as C7.

C9.note: Bypass on U1's regulated +12 V output (§2-26). Sheet 1.

C22.note: 0.22 µF ceramic in parallel with C6 on U1's input, although §2-26 describes it with the regulated side. Sheet 1. Same derived 18 V as C6.

C14.note: 0.22 µF ceramic on the unregulated +5 V rail, in parallel with C20 and C21 just ahead of TP11 and U3's input. §2-25 lists it once among the 'filter capacitors C12, C13 and C14' and once as a bypass; the sheet says both sentences describe the same node. Not a bulk filter and not a recap candidate.

C20.note: Ceramic across the +5 V reservoir, with C21, filtering the high-frequency noise C12 and C13 cannot (§2-25). Sheet 1.

C21.note: The other half of the pair with C20. Sheet 1.

C24.note: 0.022 µF 500 V ceramic across the unregulated +75 V rail with C1 and R6, filtering high-frequency noise (§2-28). Sheet 1. Derived rail voltage, as for C1.

C25.note: 0.022 µF 500 V ceramic across the unregulated +35 V rail with C3 (§2-27). Sheet 1. Derived rail voltage, as for C3.

C23.note: High-frequency filter on U3's regulated output (§2-25). Sheet 1.

C16.note: With L7, the last filter on the +5 V rail before P41 (§2-25). Sheet 1.

C17.note: 0.047 µF polypropylene straight across the 75 V ac secondary, after F1 and ahead of the CR1–CR4 bridge (§2-28). Sheet 1. It sees the winding peak in both polarities, which for a capacitor-input rectifier is the dc rail plus the rectifier drop — about 101 V on the derived 100 V rail. A 630 V part, so very heavily derated, as a suppression capacitor across a mains-derived winding should be.

C18.note: 0.047 µF polypropylene across the 35 V ac secondary, after F2 and ahead of the CR9–CR12 bridge (§2-27). Sheet 1. Same derivation as C17, on the derived 45 V rail.

C5.note: 0.1 µF ceramic from the positive ac leg to COMMON, after F3 and ahead of the CR17–CR20 rectifier. Sheet 1. §2-26 calls it a bypass for the regulated +12 V supply, but the sheet puts it on the ac side. Sees the winding peak, about the same magnitude as the derived 18 V rail.

C19.note: 0.22 µF ceramic from the negative ac leg to COMMON, after F4 — the mirror of C5. Sheet 1. §2-26 groups it with the -12 V output bypasses; the sheet puts it on the ac side.

C11.note: 0.1 µF ceramic across the 5 V ac secondary, after F5 and the common-mode choke L8, ahead of the CR25–CR28 bridge (§2-25). Sheet 1. Sees the winding peak, about the derived 8.5 V rail plus the rectifier drop.
